speaker: SPEAKER_01
transcript: Senator Rand Paul had called for a procedural vote regarding the constitutionality of the effort to impeach Trump for a second time, filed by the House, since Trump is now out of office. The Republican Kentucky Senator tweeted, The Senate just voted on my constitutional point of order. 45 senators agreed that this sham of a trial is unconstitutional. That is more than will be needed to acquit and to eventually end this partisan impeachment process. According to Paul, this trial is dead on arrival in the Senate. Paul also told reporters, if you voted that it was unconstitutional, how in the world would you ever vote to convict somebody for this? This vote indicates it's over. The trial is all over. House Democrats accused Trump of incitement of insurrection in the January 6th Capitol Hill riot, voting in favor of the impeachment without holding hearings and sending the vote to the Senate, where a trial could disqualify him from office. Senator James Langford, a Republican from Oklahoma, said in a press release, This is not a trial. This is political theater. You cannot remove someone from office who is already out of office. The U.S. Constitution outlines the process for impeachment and trial of the president, but it says nothing about trying a former president. Since Trump is no longer president, Chief Justice John Roberts won't preside over the impeachment trial should it occur. Instead, according to the Hill, Senator Patrick Leahy, a Democrat from Vermont, will preside. Paul had a comment about that as well. He tweeted, If Chief Justice Roberts can't be bothered to come over for the so-called impeachment, makes you wonder if this exercise is constitutional at all. According to CNN, Paul said Tuesday that he forced the procedural vote to show there already aren't sufficient votes to convict Trump, which would require two-thirds of senators.

The House did not hold hearings before voting to impeach and sent the matter directly to the Senate.
According to the U.S. Constitution, there is no provision for impeaching a former president.
Paul stated that 45 senators agreeing the trial is unconstitutional means it is unlikely to result in conviction.
Since Trump is no longer president, Chief Justice John Roberts will not preside over any potential trial.
Paul claimed the trial is 'dead on arrival' in the Senate.
Paul argued that if senators found the trial unconstitutional, they couldn’t logically vote to convict.

assumptions.text: Two-thirds of senators are required to convict in an impeachment trial.
A trial lacking constitutional basis lacks legitimacy and should not proceed.
Senators who believe something is unconstitutional are less likely to vote to convict.
The outcome of a procedural vote reflects genuine legislative intent rather than mere formality.
Political motivations undermine the credibility of the impeachment process when conducted post-presidency.
Impeachment trials should follow strict adherence to constitutional procedures to maintain public trust.
